failure_analysis.what: Combined primary 1473.206 us/op > baseline 1336.029 us/op (+10.3%). age_createEdge=8372.231 us/op and neo4j_createEdge=4296.258 us/op (with large error bars +/-8992) both regressed; other sub-scores are in normal range.
failure_analysis.why: Transaction/session batching did not remove round-trips. In AGE, the outer Exposed transaction still issues each createVertex/createEdge as a separate SQL exec() call; holding the connection longer increased variance against HikariCP connectionInitSql overhead. In Neo4j, the shared Session via ThreadLocal did not reduce Bolt round-trips because each s.run() is still one server trip; session open/close is inexpensive relative to query RTT, so reusing it yielded no speedup while introducing warmup variance.
failure_analysis.lesson: Transaction/session-level batching only helps when the driver actually pipelines or batches statements. Both Exposed JDBC and the Neo4j Bolt driver execute each statement as its own round-trip. To cut createEdge latency, future planners should merge the 3 ops into a SINGLE statement (e.g., one Cypher MERGE/CREATE that creates both nodes and the edge in a single query, or a single AGE SQL with multiple Cypher clauses). Do not target tx/session lifecycle grouping for latency wins.
